transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE); Raj Patel (Clearline Head of Platform); Lena Moretti (ML Eng); Tom Diaz (CTO)
Shared: deck: https://redwood.example/deck/hosted-demo, demo repo: https://github.com/redwood/example-streaming

---
[00:00:05] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Quick intro from Daniel on the SE side.
[00:00:12] Daniel: Hi all, Daniel Ortiz, I'll run through the live demo focusing on streaming and generation params, and then we'll cover retries and rate-limit behavior.
[00:00:22] Raj: Thanks, we just want to see how streaming works and what knobs we can use to control hallucination vs latency. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated.
[00:00:30] Tom: From our side low latency and PII handling are the two big items. We'll want to see how tokens are billed too.

[00:01:05] Daniel: Great. High level: Redwood Hosted API supports chat, text generation, embeddings, re-ranking. For chat we show a sample streaming flow with server-sent events (SSE) or webhooks for chunking. Demo will use streaming SSE.
[00:01:35] Daniel: (shares screen) Here's the curl example: POST /v1/chat with stream=true. You open a chunked connection and we flush tokens as they are generated. Typical event format is incremental text and token-level metadata.
[00:02:10] Lena: Sorry, could you show the param list again? I want to see how temperature and top_p interplay.
[00:02:18] Daniel: Sure. We have temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, and presence/frequency penalties. Temperature controls randomness; top_p is nucleus sampling. We usually recommend starting with temp 0.2-0.6 for assistant style. For determinism set temp=0 and top_p=1.
[00:02:45] Daniel: Also a note on streaming and token costs: we charge on tokens generated + input tokens, streaming doesn't change billing model.

[00:03:20] Maya: Quick qualification: what's your expected QPS and typical prompt lengths?
[00:03:28] Raj: For pilot maybe 20 QPS peak, average prompt 80-150 tokens, responses ~120 tokens. We'll need <200ms tail latency per token ideally.
[00:03:40] Daniel: That's helpful. For that profile hosted should be fine but we can also discuss Dedicated for stricter SLOs. We do batch at the runtime level, so per-token latency depends on batching window and kernel choices.

[00:04:30] Daniel: Live demo: I'm going to send a chat request with stream=true. You should see incremental events.
[00:04:45] Daniel: (runs command)
[00:05:00] Redwood-stream: data: {"delta": "Hello"}
[00:05:02] Raj: Nice, that's pretty snappy. Do you expose chunk size?
[00:05:10] Daniel: Chunking is about flush frequency - we let runtime decide for efficiency but you can tune 'token_flush_ms' via request-level hint to influence latency vs efficiency tradeoff (note: this is a recommended hint not a strict SLA).

[00:06:05] Lena: How do retries look? If we get a 5xx mid-stream what happens?
[00:06:10] Daniel: Good question. For transient 5xx we recommend client-side idempotency via request_id; the platform supports resume from last good token in some cases, else you re-issue the request. For network errors or 429, our SDKs implement exponential backoff and jitter. We surface final status events so you can detect incomplete streams.
[00:06:40] Daniel: Example: send request with x-request-id header; if you need at-most-once semantics use idempotency keys plus server-side dedupe.

[00:07:20] Tom: About rate-limits - will we hit 429 at 20 QPS? Also do you support burst windows?
[00:07:28] Maya: Hosted accounts have rate-limits based on plan; we can configure higher per-customer quotas. We also support short burst capacity; Dedicated gives fixed throughput. We'll share the quota table in the pricing doc.

[00:08:15] Daniel: Back to params: another important one is response_length control - max_tokens and stop sequences are key for preventing over-generation in prompts like card numbers. Use stop sequences to cut if you have structured outputs.
[00:08:45] Lena: For PII, does Redwood persist prompts/outputs? We have PCI concerns.
[00:08:52] Maya: By default Hosted retains logs for troubleshooting but customers can opt-out or request shorter retention. For PCI-level needs we'd recommend either Dedicated with encryption + KMS or Private with on-prem. We also offer contract options for data residency and dedicated log retention policies.

[00:09:30] Raj: So if we start with Hosted for pilot, what's the path to Dedicated?
[00:09:35] Maya: Smooth path: same API surface, you can pin model versions and move to Dedicated later. We handle model variants and routing. We'll include a migration checklist in the follow-ups.

[00:10:20] Daniel: Demo: now toggling temperature from 0.7 to 0.2, same prompt. Notice fewer diversions in streaming text and earlier stop.
[00:11:00] Redwood-stream: data: {"delta":"...","meta":{"token_id":112}}
[00:11:10] Raj: Small question - do you do prefix caching / KV cache for multi-turn dialogues?
[00:11:18] Daniel: Yes, we do prefix and KV cache to reduce redundant compute. For chat-heavy flows we recommend using conversation-level cache hints and also upload canonical context for cold-starts. There are context window tradeoffs; we can evict or snapshot KV cache between requests.

[00:12:05] Lena: Any SDKs? We want Java + node.
[00:12:08] Daniel: Yes, JS, Python, Java examples. The streaming SDK handles reconnects for SSE and gives you token events. I'll share code snippet after.

[00:12:45] Maya: Quick objection we often hear: what about cost vs OpenAI?
[00:12:52] Raj: yes that's part of our evaluation.
[00:12:55] Daniel: Cost depends on model choice and quantization. We show comparative perf profiles in the catalog. Also Optimize gives batching and cache recommendations to reduce per-token cost.

[00:13:40] Daniel: Now show retry example: simulate 5xx by returning early - SDK logs show retry attempts with backoff; we surface event that stream was incomplete.
[00:14:05] Daniel: (shows logs) retry-attempt 1, 2, success on 3.
[00:14:12] Tom: Good, do you keep trace ids so we can join with our logs?
[00:14:17] Maya: Yes we pass request IDs and trace headers; you can correlate via trace id. We also export traces into your SIEM via webhook.

[00:15:00] Daniel: A dev tip: for interactive UIs, render tokens as they arrive and buffer punctuation to reduce jitter. Also use partials to highlight confidence.

[00:15:45] Lena: For model selection, do you recommend open models or Redwood-curated ones?
[00:15:50] Daniel: Depends on use case; our catalog lists curated open models with performance profiles. For payment chat, safety-tuned variants or applying post-processing filters for PANs/PII is recommended. We can show evals on similar workloads.

[00:17:00] Raj: We need SOC2 and encryption details.
[00:17:05] Maya: We'll send the security pack - SOC2, ISO, KMS integration, audit logs; for Hosted we support customer-managed keys in some tiers.

[00:18:10] Daniel: Walkthrough of the console: you can monitor token breakdown, per-route latency, error spikes, and set alerts. Also rollout controls for model versions.
[00:18:40] Daniel: (shows console screenshots) Here is per-token cost heatmap, and here is a streaming session inspector with token timestamps.

[00:19:50] Tom: If we see degradation, do you have fallbacks?
[00:19:55] Daniel: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to cheaper or more available model variants, plus regional fallbacks. You can configure fallbacks per-route.

[00:21:10] Raj: For the pilot we want to measure latency, error rate, and cost per 1M tokens. Can you provide an estimate?
[00:21:20] Maya: We'll send a pricing estimate based on your traffic profile. Daniel will include a benchmark run template so you can run locally against a sample traffic file.

[00:22:00] Daniel: Quick Q: Do you need streaming binary attachments or just text?
[00:22:05] Raj: Just text for now, maybe later attachments for receipts.

[00:23:10] Daniel: Demo wrap-up: reiterate streaming best practices - use client-side reconnect with idempotency key, tune token_flush_ms for latency, set max_tokens and stop sequences for structured outputs, and use Optimize suggestions to reduce cost.

[00:24:00] Lena: Any gotchas for tokenization differences? We saw mismatch in char counts when moving from our tokenizer to the model.
[00:24:07] Daniel: Yes tokenization differences exist across model families; we publish tokenizers in the model catalog and you can run a tokenization pre-check in your CI.

[00:25:20] Maya: Recap & next steps: we'll send pricing + security pack, Daniel to share code snippets + streaming repo, you (Raj/Lena) to share sample prompts and traffic. Plan pilot kickoff next week.

[00:26:05] Raj: Sounds good. One more - do you support strict no-logging for host data?
[00:26:12] Maya: We can set stricter retention or opt-out in contract for Hosted; Dedicated/Private are recommended for absolute isolation.

[00:27:00] Tom: Ok we're aligned, thanks.

[00:27:30] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with action items.

[00:28:00] (call ends)
